title: Shortest Palindrome
summary: Given a string s , determine the shortest palindrome by appending characters to the front of s .
statement: Given a string s , determine the shortest palindrome by appending characters to the front of s .
constraints: Add characters ONLY before the original string. Return the shortest resulting palindrome, preserving the original string as a suffix. Empty input returns an empty string.
hints: The part of the original string that need not be mirrored is a palindromic prefix.
Find the longest palindromic prefix, then prepend the reversed remaining suffix.
Build the prefix-function for s + a separator + reverse(s); its final value is the longest palindromic-prefix length.
Choose a separator outside lowercase letters. Prefix-function fallback avoids repeatedly rescanning long almost-matching prefixes.
editorial: If the longest palindromic prefix has length p, mirroring the remaining suffix in front produces a palindrome using n-p added characters. Fewer added characters would imply a longer palindromic prefix, so this is minimal. The prefix-function on s#reverse(s) finds p in linear time because the separator cannot occur in s. The independent oracle scans candidate prefixes directly for palindromicity; an additional small-domain test enumerates possible prepended strings to verify minimality without assuming the prefix theorem.

tests.explanation: Its longest palindromic prefix is 'aacecaa'; prepend the reverse of the remaining 'a' to obtain 'aaacecaaa'.
Only the initial 'a' is a palindromic prefix; prepend 'dcb' to get 'dcbabcd'. Appending characters is not allowed.
